$comment: The behaviour suite's CI time budget (#71, FR-013, NFR-001).
The charter's Performance Benchmarks say 'Storybook CI build time under 3 minutes' and
contemplate no test suite at all - ADR-11's own Consequences say 'a new budget has to be
set rather than assumed'. This is that budget, ASSERTED rather than recorded: both jobs
fail above their ceiling, so neither number can go stale silently.
There is deliberately NO `measuredSeconds` field. An earlier revision carried 5.6, which
was contradicted by the very run it cited (6.8s) and by head (11.9s) - a companion number
that nothing re-derives is the prose baseline this whole file argues against. The ceilings
are the record.
TWO ceilings, because they measure different things and mixing them could not tell you
which had regressed. `ceilingSeconds` covers `npm run test` - both lanes, chromium and
webkit in CI. `selftestCeilingSeconds` covers scripts/suite-selftest.mjs, which proves a
complete full-suite baseline and runs every dependency-affected browser test per mutation.
That second key was
read by NOTHING until the second gate pass caught it: an inert key documented as an
enforced ceiling, in the file whose thesis is that stale prose goes unnoticed.
At #146 Vitest's unmutated dependency graph replaced the mutation-registry-derived filter.
Package barrels remain broad; graph errors and empty selections fail closed to the full suite,
and every run matches its affected SC assertion set. Exact-head CI run 34031816773 then proved
that filtering was active (29 sources, zero full-suite fallbacks) and every one of 128 mutations
produced its named red against a green 307-assertion baseline, but 923.9s exceeded 881.9s.
The operator authorized remediation on 2026-09-06. The ceiling is therefore recalibrated to
1405.5s using the repository's existing 1.5213x worst-observed-CI multiplier:
923.9 x (881.9 / 579.7) = 1405.5s. This retains 52.1% headroom over the new worst run.
The 568.6s workstation result is recorded only as a 62.5% CI/local variance observation; CI
remains authoritative. One CI observation does not prove the runner tail, so a future breach
must trigger investigation rather than another automatic raise.

ceilingSeconds RAISED AT #233, 25 -> 38.3, ON MEASURED GROWTH RATHER THAN ON VARIANCE, by the operator ruling of 2026-09-07. THE THREE MEASUREMENTS, all on code that did not change: run 34063224583 (7b446d7, a docs-only branch) measured 25.2s and FAILED; the `gh run rerun --failed` of that same SHA measured 18s and passed; run 34064899152 (1d03584, one docs-only commit later) measured 22.9s. 762 of 762 assertions passed in the failing run — the red was the budget line alone, on a pull request that changed only Markdown. THE POINT IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE OUTLIER: the distribution STRADDLED the old ceiling rather than sitting under it (18 / 22.9 / 25.2 against 25), so the same tree passed or failed on which runner it landed on. A gate that decides on runner allocation invites re-running until green, which is worse than one that fails honestly; that is the same argument the 560 -> 881.9 raise records for selftestCeilingSeconds at a different scale, and it is why this is a raise rather than a re-roll.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE VARIANCE-DRIVEN RAISE #187 WARNED AGAINST. The suite GREW. 25 was measured at 0f1df74 (run 33713144837) and the only ordinary-behaviour-gate figure this file records since — the note on the 28917cc selftest row below — has it passing 647/647 in 22.5s. The three measurements above are 762 tests. That is +115 tests, +17.8%, against a ceiling that never moved. THE ARITHMETIC, stated so it can be checked rather than trusted: worst observed x the repository's own worst-observed multiplier, 1.5213 — the figure the 360 -> 560 raise established (560 / 368.1) and the 560 -> 881.9 and 881.9 -> 1405.5 raises both reused. 25.2 x 1.5213 = 38.3s. That is 52.1% headroom over the WORST run seen (38.3 / 25.2), not over the average. Against the FASTEST of the three it is 113% (38.3 / 18) — stated because an earlier revision of this sentence said 67.4%, which is 38.3 / 22.9, the MIDDLE run, mislabelled as the fastest. Caught by a pre-merge lens, and recorded rather than quietly corrected: this file's whole claim is that its arithmetic can be checked instead of trusted, and the check found it. NOT ROUNDED to 40: a round number is a number nobody can re-derive, and this file already records two occasions on which its own arithmetic was falsified by the very next run.

THE TEST COUNT KEEPS MOVING, AND THAT IS THE POINT — the next reader has to tell growth from variance the way this ruling did, and cannot do it from one number. #233's three measurements are at 762 tests, on 7b446d7 (PR #230). The train has grown since: at 7e181a9 the same count is 764 (34 node + 365 browser, and CI runs the browser lane on BOTH chromium and webkit, which is why the browser half doubles). This mission (#196/#204) adds exactly ONE browser test, so it lands at 766 — predicted as arithmetic from a chromium-only workstation run, then MEASURED on CI rather than left as a prediction: run 34068676458 (d048760) reports `node=34 browser (chromium)=366 browser (webkit)=366` and `suite wall-clock: 19.6s (ceiling 38.3s)`. 766, as derived. The figure to compare a future breach against is 38.3s at 766 tests, and there are now TWO observations under it, on the same PR and the same 766 tests: 19.6s at d048760 and 24.3s at 5fb9794. The PAIR is the point rather than either number — a 24% spread on an identical test set, the slower of the two landing 0.7s under the OLD 25s ceiling, which is the straddle this raise exists to end, reproduced on this very branch. A raise asked for at a count that has not moved is a variance raise, not a growth one.

WHY 40 STANDS RATHER THAN 38.3. Lowering a ceiling another mission raised on its own exact-head measurement would cut #148's margin from 43% to 37% over its 28.0s run, for no gain: the #233 ruling asks for a figure ABOVE the observed tail with the headroom stated, and 40 is above it — 58.7% over the 25.2s tail — with the headroom stated here. The 1.5213 arithmetic stays on the record as the FLOOR it derived, so a future reader can see the ruling was satisfied by a number rather than waived. selftestCeilingSeconds IS NOT TOUCHED BY #233 and stays at 1405.5. It is #225's, it waits for the filtered-suite redesign, and the preamble above keeps the two keys apart precisely because mixing them could not tell you which had regressed. The 25 -> 38.3 raise here says nothing about the mutation harness, and no reader should infer that it does.
WHERE THIS BUDGET LIVES IS AN OPEN OPERATOR QUESTION. Amending the charter's Performance
Benchmarks may be the right home, but charter.md and charter.yaml contradict each other and
ADR-11's citation for how amendments happen does not check out - see the operator questions
adds the mutations rather than to the end of the mission — the ceiling asserts at the end of
EVERY run and is wired into CI, so it reds at whichever commit pushes the set over, not at a
tidy final measurement pass.

MEASURED AGAIN at #126: 43 mutations / 83 browser tests -> 161.1s CI, 18.9s under the 180s ceiling. That is roughly five more mutations of headroom at the true marginal cost, NOT the "roughly four" this paragraph used to claim from the 41-mutation row.
The harness spawns vitest with `CI: ''`, so it is chromium-only; the second browser affects
`ceilingSeconds` (npm run test), not this one. The two are kept separate so a regression can
be attributed.
DELIBERATE, AND RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS A TRADE-OFF: #74 added 18 tests and only 2
standing mutations. Thirteen more survivors were each proven red-first by hand during the
gate fold, but adding them to the standing set would cost ~130s and breach the ceiling. The
next mission to touch this file should raise selftestCeilingSeconds deliberately, with the
run that justifies it, rather than discover the breach.

THE SLOPE, corrected. #74 recorded "~10s per added mutation" and #126 planned around it. That figure bundles two variables: the harness runs one FULL SUITE per mutation, so the two committed CI points (39 mut/62 tests -> 121.7s; 41/80 -> 141.6s) fit per-run ~= 1.90s + 0.0183s x tests. A mutation with no new tests costs ~3.4s; the 10s was a mutation PLUS nine tests. #126 predicted 151s on that fit and CI measured 161.1s, so the model under-predicts by ~7% — good enough to plan with, not good enough to quote.

NOT RAISED at #126, deliberately. Two mutations were added and the run still fits with 18.9s spare, so raising the ceiling would have been raising it from an arithmetic the run does not support — the defect this file records a lens catching twice. The next mission to add mutations should expect to raise it, and now has a real slope to do that from.

TWO POINTS AT THE SAME COUNTS, 161.1s and 155.5s, both CI, both 43 mutations / 83 tests. That spread is runner variance, and it is recorded rather than averaged away: a single quoted figure is what this file exists to argue against. Plan against the SLOWER one.

RAISED AT #77, 180 -> 240, which is the deliberate raise the paragraph above told the next mission adding mutations to expect. The justifying run is the breach itself: CI @ a1a0623, 47 mutations / 91 browser tests, harness step 23:26:15Z -> 23:29:15Z — it ran to completion, every mutation produced its named red, and the ONLY failure was this ceiling. That is recorded as a measurement row with seconds 180 and a `ceilingBreach` flag, because the exact elapsed is known only to be marginally above 180: the script prints its own figure and CI truncated the log at the failure. THE ARITHMETIC, stated so it can be checked rather than trusted: the committed fit is per-run ~= 1.90s + 0.0183s x tests, so predicted(47, 91) = 167.6s against an actual of ~180 — the ~7% under-prediction this file already records, here measured at ~7.4%. predicted(49, 98) = 181.0s; scaled by the same factor, ~194s. Runner variance is ~3.6% at identical counts (161.1 vs 155.5 above), so ~202s is the number to plan against. 240 leaves ~19% headroom, which is roughly ten mutations at the true marginal cost. NOT SET TO ~205. A ceiling with no headroom converts ordinary runner variance into a red build on a tree nobody touched, and the next mission would spend its gate pass re-raising it. NO LOCAL FIGURE IS QUOTED AS THE BASIS. This mission's workstation run was 138.9s at 49/98, which is 30% under CI and is exactly the kind of number a lens has twice caught this file citing as though it were binding.

THE 240 ARITHMETIC WAS WRONG, and the very next CI run said so. The paragraph above predicted ~194s at 49 mutations and planned 240 around it. CI @ bcef5a3 measured 49 mutations / 100 browser tests at 128.5s — 34% under the prediction, and 52s FASTER than the a1a0623 run that breached 180s with TWO FEWER mutations. So the interpretation of that breach changes: it was not the mutation count crossing a threshold, it was a slow runner. Runner variance across these two adjacent runs is at least 180 -> 128.5, roughly 40% of the mean — an order of magnitude beyond the ~3.6% recorded above from the 161.1/155.5 pair, which was evidently a lucky pair rather than the spread. The per-run fit (1.90s + 0.0183s x tests) should not be used to plan a ceiling. It predicts a central tendency and the ceiling has to survive the tail. 240 STAYS, on the corrected basis: it is ~1.9x the fastest observed run at this count and ~1.33x the slowest observed run at any count, which is headroom for the variance actually measured rather than for the slope. A ceiling derived from the fit would have been ~205 and would red on a slow runner with nothing wrong. Recorded rather than quietly corrected, because a prediction contradicted by the next run is exactly the shape this file exists to catch, and it caught mine.

RAISED AGAIN AT #78, 240 -> 360, and this time the measurement came FIRST. A lens refused the PR body's '212.8s local vs 240s' as evidence — correctly, since this file says twice that a workstation figure is not ceiling-relevant — and asked for the CI number before merge. It is 231.7s at 54 mutations / 116 tests: 8.3s of headroom, not the comfortable margin the local figure implied. AND THE VARIANCE IS LARGER THAN ANY MODEL HERE. Adjacent CI runs: 128.5s at 49/100, 231.7s at 54/116. The work grew ~28% (mutations x tests) and the time grew ~80%. Whatever the per-run fit predicts, the spread between two runs five days apart is the number a ceiling has to survive, and this file's own conclusion says so. 360 is ~1.55x the slowest observed run at the current count. It is not derived from the fit, which under-predicts and describes a central tendency. #79 adds a third batch of components and should re-measure rather than assume this holds.

RAISED AT #77 PART 3, 360 -> 560, and for once the marginal cost is measured rather than fitted. Three CI runs on ONE DAY, same runner class, backfilled below: 64 mut/144 tests -> 300.6s, 67/154 -> 319.1s, 70/160 -> 368.1s. Two of those three rows were owed by earlier missions and never written — #79 was told in this file to re-measure and did not, so the 360 ceiling stood on #78's 54-mutation figure while the standing set grew to 67 unobserved. That is the defect this file exists to catch, committed against this file's own instruction, by me.

WHY 560 AND NOT 480. 480 is 1.30x the slowest observed run and looks generous against a same-day cluster that spans only 300.6-368.1s. It is not, and this file already records why: the widest variance ever measured here is a1a0623 (>180s at 47/91) against bcef5a3 (128.5s at 49/100) — adjacent runs, MORE work in the faster one, ~40% apart. A 40%-slow runner at today's count is ~515s, which 480 would red with nothing wrong. 560 is 1.52x the slowest observed, consistent with the 1.55x basis #78 used, and survives the worst variance actually recorded. The tight same-day cluster is NOT evidence the fleet got more consistent; it is three samples, and this file has twice been wrong by treating a central tendency as a bound.

THE REAL PROBLEM IS NOT THE CEILING, and raising it is treating a symptom. suite-selftest.mjs runs the WHOLE suite once per mutation, so cost is O(mutations x tests) and BOTH factors grow every migration mission — which is why 6 mutations and 16 tests cost 67.5s here while the committed per-run fit predicts a fraction of that. The harness is now over six minutes and each mission has raised this number: 180 -> 240 -> 360 -> 560. The next raise should not happen; the harness should mutate against a filtered suite instead. Filed rather than fixed here, because changing what the harness runs changes what every red means and that is not a fold at the end of a component migration.

MEASURED AT #81 WITHOUT RAISING ANYTHING: 70 mutations / 166 tests -> 364s. The set grew by six tests and the time did not move outside variance (368.1s at 160 tests). Recorded because this file's standing instruction is to re-measure when the mutation set OR the test set grows, and a lens caught that #81 had grown the test set and written nothing down. Re-measuring and declining to raise is the outcome this instruction wants; silence is not.

RECHECKED AT #180's SECOND ROUND, NOT RAISED — the breach is explained, not fixed. CI @ 33996545427 (9dc04f2), 92 mutations / 233 tests, 579.7s: 19.7s over the 560s ceiling. Per-mutation cost: 6.234s (mean gap across all 92 timestamped results, stdev 0.088s — EVERY mutation in this run cost within 1.4% of the mean; there is no disproportionately slow arm, checked by measuring the gap between each of the 92 result lines individually, not inferred). Two things explain the total, neither of them a code defect: (1) CI-vs-local overhead — this mission's own local run was 381.9s/92 = 4.15s/mutation, so CI ran ~52% slower than the workstation, in line with the ~30-43% CI-vs-local gap #78 already recorded ("this mission's workstation run was 138.9s at 49/98, which is 30% under CI"), not a new phenomenon. (2) CI-to-CI variance — the immediately preceding CI row (cde2fb8, 85mut/224tests, 358.6s = 4.22s/mutation) is 33% CHEAPER per mutation than this run, almost exactly the ~40-46% swing already recorded between a1a0623 (>180s @ 47/91, ~3.83s/mutation) and bcef5a3 (128.5s @ 49/100, ~2.62s/mutation) — a RECURRENCE of already-documented runner variance at a different scale, not a new one. NOT RAISED because the file's own #77-part-3 note (PR #166, 75ca61e) already told this exact next mission not to: "the next raise should not happen; the harness should mutate against a filtered suite instead." This mission's own growth (70->92 mutations, 169->233 tests over its lifetime) is precisely the growth that note anticipated. A ceiling raise here would be technically computable (roughly 1.5x this run's total, ~870-900s, matching the 1.52-1.55x buffer-over-worst-observed-run basis #77/#78 used) and would make this specific red go away, but it would be the FOURTH consecutive mission-by-mission raise (240->360->560->~900) the file's own standing note already flagged as the wrong move. Left for the operator: raise again on this basis, or invest in the filtered-suite harness redesign #77-part-3 (PR #166) filed instead of fixed.

RAISED AT #180, 560 -> 881.9s, OPERATOR OVERRIDE of the #77-part-3 note above (PR #166, 75ca61e) (which is NOT deleted or edited — it still stands, and its recommendation is DEFERRED, not rejected: the filtered-suite redesign remains the right fix; this raise buys time, it does not close it). This is the FOURTH consecutive raise (180 -> 240 -> 360 -> 560 -> 881.9), and that note said the next one should not happen — it did not happen on this loop's own authority. Ruled by the operator on 2026-09-06 in #187, recorded here so the next reader knows the decision was escalated rather than assumed, the same treatment ADR-10 got in #176. THE ARITHMETIC, same basis as the 360->560 raise (worst observed CI run x buffer, not a fit to the central tendency): that raise was 1.52x its own worst observed run (560 / 368.1 = 1.5213). Applied to THIS mission's worst observed run (579.7s, 9dc04f2, recorded above): 579.7 x 1.5213 = 881.9s. Not rounded to a clean number and back-filled — the multiplier is the SAME one already used once, applied to the new worst observation. WHY NOT A SMALLER RAISE: the finding that forced this is not the single breach, it is that at 92 mutations the suite STRADDLES a marginal ceiling — 4.22s/mutation on cde2fb8 and 6.30s/mutation on 9dc04f2 spans an expected-runtime range of roughly 390-580s against the OLD 560s ceiling, meaning the gate could pass or fail on ordinary runner variance alone with no code change either side. A gate that passes or fails on variance is worse than one that fails honestly, because it invites re-running until green rather than trusting the result. 881.9s puts the ceiling clearly ABOVE the observed 4.22-6.30s/mutation range at the current count (92 x 6.30 = 579.6, against 881.9 — 52% headroom over the WORST run seen, not the average), restoring a deterministic gate rather than a coin flip. THE PER-MUTATION SPREAD, recorded so the next mission can predict its own budget: 4.22-6.30s/mutation across two consecutive CI runs of the SAME suite (cde2fb8, 9dc04f2), while the spread WITHIN a single run is tight (stdev 0.088s on 9dc04f2's 92 results, 1.4% of the mean) — the variance is between RUNNERS, not between mutation arms. CI-VS-LOCAL, also recorded: this mission's own workstation run was 4.15s/mutation against CI's 6.30s/mutation on the same head, a ~52% gap, consistent with the ~30-43% gap #78 already recorded — a local green does not predict a CI green for this gate, budget from the CI figure, never the workstation one.

MEASURED AT #182, NOT RAISED. CI @ ddbfcc7 (run 34031680527), 111 mutations / 284 browser tests, 761.8s against the 881.9s ceiling — 6.863s/mutation, inside the 4.22-6.30s/mutation band #180 recorded only at its top end, and 86.4% of the ceiling. TWO THINGS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN ACTED ON. (1) This row is partly owed by an earlier mission: the last measurement below is 92 mutations / 233 tests, and the set had already reached 109 / 270 on the train before #182 touched it, so no row was written for that growth — the same omission this file records #79 and #81 committing, and it is named here rather than quietly backfilled, because I did not run that mission and cannot attribute its figure. (2) The margin is thin against the variance this file itself documents: 120.1s of headroom is ~14%, and the widest CI-to-CI swing recorded here is ~40% (a1a0623 >180s at 47/91 against bcef5a3 128.5s at 49/100). A 40%-slow runner at this count is ~1066s and would breach. NOT RAISED HERE, deliberately and for a stated reason rather than an arithmetic one: the 560 -> 881.9 raise was an OPERATOR RULING (2026-09-06, #187) taken because the file's own #77-part-3 note (PR #166, 75ca61e) says the next raise should not happen on a loop's own authority and that the real fix is mutating against a filtered suite. A component mission adding two mutation arms is not the place to spend that ruling a second time. The operator's options are unchanged: raise again on the same worst-observed x 1.5213 basis (761.8 x 1.5213 = 1158.9s), or fund the filtered-suite redesign. CI-VS-LOCAL, for the next reader's budgeting: this mission's workstation run was 451.5s at the same 111/284, so CI ran ~69% slower — wider than the ~52% gap #180 measured and well outside the ~30-43% #78 recorded. Budget from the CI figure; the workstation one has now been wrong by a larger margin again.

AND THE VERY NEXT RUN FALSIFIED THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE, which is recorded rather than quietly edited because a prediction contradicted by the next run is the exact shape this file exists to catch — and it has now caught mine, as it caught the 240 arithmetic. Same PR, same 111 mutations / 284 tests, one rebase later: CI @ 6189027 (run 34032506923) measured 575.6s, against 761.8s at ddbfcc7. That is a 32% spread between two ADJACENT runs of an IDENTICAL set, 4.87 vs 6.86 s/mutation — no code changed between them but a rebase onto #203, which touches no test. So the '86.4% of the ceiling, ~14% headroom' figure above is a worst-observed point, not the level: the honest statement is 575.6-761.8s, 65-86% of the ceiling. The decision does not change and the reason strengthens: a ceiling must survive the tail, the tail here is 761.8s, and 881.9 clears it — while a ceiling fitted to the 575.6s run would red on the 761.8s one with nothing wrong. What this pair adds to the record is that the ~40% CI-to-CI variance this file documents from a1a0623/bcef5a3 was NOT an artefact of differing counts: it reproduces at identical counts, on the same day, on the same PR.

RAISED AT #148, 25 -> 40, from exact-head CI rather than a workstation result. PR #231 run 34064831840 at eabbb844 completed all 798 assertions across node, Chromium, and WebKit with zero skips in 28.0s; the only test-job failure was the old 25s ceiling. The last recorded ordinary-suite point was #146 at 647 assertions in 22.5s. Assertions therefore grew 23.3% and elapsed time grew 24.4%, with #148's own sk-bar-chart contract green in both browsers (15/15 each); that proportional change is suite growth, not a hung or isolated slow test. Two immediately preceding runs of the identical 798-assertion floor measured 23.6s at 18f16cdd (run 34063650759) and 23.5s at 3b42fa00 (run 34064628144), so the old ceiling had only about 6% headroom on ordinary runs and the 28.0s result demonstrates same-count runner variance rather than a reason to rerun until lucky. Forty seconds is 1.43x the measured worst run and leaves 30% of the ceiling as runner headroom. The distinct 1,405.5s mutation ceiling is unchanged and still requires its own final-head CI measurement.
